clue.text: Editors of baseball's first World Series broadcast

indicators.note: the first letter of the word baseball's is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of World Series are strewn into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about who edited the radio or TV coverage of the very first baseball World Series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like it belongs to the sports coverage, but it is the anagram signal. Thomas Bowdler expurgated Shakespeare, giving us the verb bowdlerise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowdlerisers are people who censor texts by cutting anything offensive, a particular kind of editor.

clue.text: Really great booze stocked by bar close to Reading

indicators.note: the booze is held in stock inside the other letters, so it goes within them

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: only its final letter is used
gin is a spirit, a classic word for booze

explanation.surface: A pub near Reading keeps some really excellent drink on its shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the English town, but here only its last letter counts. Banging is British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British slang, banging describes something excellent, as in a banging tune.

clue.text: They're made with lots of time

parts.note: ages is an informal way of saying a long time

explanation.surface: A cryptic-sounding remark that something takes a great deal of time to produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole reads like a cryptic definition, but the split is 'They're made' as definition and the rest as wordplay; wages are what one 'makes' at work.
explanation.definitionFit: People speak of making a living, so earnings or pay are what workers make.

clue.text: Free places to go in the summer in France

indicators.note: the toilets are placed in the French phrase, inside its letters

parts.note: French l'été means 'the summer'
a loo is a toilet, the place to go when nature calls

explanation.surface: Free holiday spots to visit in France during the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places to go' suggests holiday destinations; it means toilets. Loo is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To let loose is to release or set at liberty, a verb phrase matching free as a verb.

clue.text: Banter is, like, enveloped in nonsense

indicators.note: the word for like is wrapped up inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
as can mean like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Someone noting that banter is, like, wrapped up in nonsense, in a casual speaking style.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'like' looks like a verbal filler; it is the piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a comic event of affectionate mockery, and to roast someone is to tease them, a form of banter.

clue.text: Choice of meals frequently ignored, in part

indicators.note: the two letters are placed in the word for part

parts.note: a section is a part of something

indicators.note: every other letter of meals is ignored, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: only its second and fourth letters survive

explanation.surface: A menu offering a choice of meals, often skipped or only partly eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice of meals' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Choice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is the act of picking or the range on offer, a synonym for a choice.

clue.text: Back off, it's about time to give up?

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season when people give up a luxury

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether backing off means it is time to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give up' sounds like surrender, but it points to the Lenten custom of abstaining from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to ease off or soften one's stance, which is to back off.

clue.text: Australian soldier stationed in quiet, mostly distant West Coast city

indicators.note: the soldier is posted inside the shortened word for distant
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: aloof means distant or standoffish
A is an abbreviation for Australia or Australian
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: An Australian soldier posted in a quiet, far-off city on America's West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo Alto is a city in California, home of Stanford University, on the US Pacific coast.

clue.text: No gun-toting Americans protect the First Lady?

indicators.note: the gun lobby's letters surround and so protect the first woman

parts.note: the NRA is the National Rifle Association, the US gun lobby
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Should no armed Americans guard the President's wife?
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like the president's wife; it is Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Never a, as in 'never a word', is an emphatic way of saying no or not one.

clue.text: When it gets dark, almost everybody hides stuff occasionally

indicators.note: the two words together conceal the picked letters between them

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
all means everyone

indicators.note: only now and then is a letter taken, so alternate letters are used

parts.note: its second and fourth letters are used

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone sometimes stashes their belongings out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost everybody' reads as one idea, but it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the time of evening when darkness comes, so it is when it gets dark.

clue.text: Rent out large facility

parts.note: facility can mean ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A landlord letting out a big building or facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' suggests a building; here it means effortlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease a property is to let it to a tenant for payment, which is renting it out.

clue.text: Popular person stealing hearts, briefly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the person takes the heart symbol and holds it inside

parts.note: a sort is a kind of person, as in a good sort
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A charming, popular figure who briefly wins people's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stealing hearts' sounds romantic, but it means taking the card abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is an idiom meaning to sum up or put concisely, the same as briefly.

clue.text: Switch, perhaps, and offer comfort

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a games machine, of which the Nintendo Switch is an example
second meaning: to comfort someone in distress

explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb or an electrical device; it is Nintendo's games machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a gaming device like the Nintendo Switch; the verb means to soothe or cheer someone who is sad.

clue.text: Musical effects represented as sliding?

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Musical effects described as sliding from note to note.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder describes the answer too, since a glissando is a slide between notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are slides up or down a scale in music, a type of musical effect; the word is the Italian plural.

clue.text: Pub drinks picked up for members of a clique

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: an inn is a pub and ciders are apple drinks, so the phrase gives inn ciders

explanation.surface: Pub drinks being collected, perhaps by a group of regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests collecting the drinks; it signals the sound of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Insiders are people within an exclusive group with privileged access, the members of a clique.

clue.text: Potentially award-winning foreign drama made money outside America

parts.note: No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: the word for made money goes outside America's letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to mint coins is to make money, so minted

explanation.surface: A foreign film tipped for awards that earned money abroad rather than in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign drama' suggests a film; it is Japanese Noh theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominated film is on an awards shortlist, so it could still win.

clue.text: From the outset, Federer's looking exhausted, and it sucks!

indicators.note: at the outset of each word, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used
only its first letter is used
only its first letter is used
only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Roger Federer looks tired from the start of the match, and that's awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It sucks' reads as slang for 'it is bad'; it literally means a creature that sucks blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a parasitic insect that feeds by sucking the blood of its host.

clue.text: Inhibited French queen ultimately stayed at home

parts.note: reine is French for queen

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its final letter is used
in means at home

explanation.surface: A shy French queen ended up staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last letter of 'stayed' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Reined in means restrained or held back, as a horse is by its reins, so inhibited.

clue.text: Bread from store delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the word for store is taken as spoken

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: Bread from a shop being brought to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like a loaf from the store; it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and cash is money in notes and coins.

clue.text: Whine about phone software that's rubbish

indicators.note: the whine goes about the phone program, surrounding it

parts.note: to cry is to whine or complain
an app is a program for a phone

explanation.surface: Complaining about a phone app that's terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Crappy is vulgar slang for poor quality, worthless or bad.

clue.text: Jeez, please leave something healthy to eat!

parts.note: Man! is an exclamation of surprise or exasperation, like Jeez!
get out is a blunt order to leave

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to go away and eat something healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to be one exasperated speech; it splits into an exclamation and an order to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout are flat pea pods eaten whole, a green vegetable and so a healthy food.

clue.text: Extremely round betel nuts became measurably bigger?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged
the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only its outer letters are used
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Round betel nuts swelled noticeably in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like part of 'betel nuts'; it is the anagram signal. 'Measurably' is fair because the growth is exactly threefold.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebled means multiplied by three, a precise and so measurable increase in size.

clue.text: Ring grabbed by sweet, tailless monkey

indicators.note: the ring is held by the sweet, inside its letters
the final letter, its tail, is cut off

parts.note: a bonbon is a sweet or candy
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A monkey with no tail snatching a ring from a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless monkey' seems to describe an ape, but 'tailless' works on the sweet. Strictly a bonobo is an ape, loosely called a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonobo is a great ape of the Congo, close kin to the chimpanzee, loosely termed a monkey.

clue.text: Unknown writer collecting military award, etc

indicators.note: the writer's name collects the award, holding it inside

parts.note: Anon, short for anonymous, is the author of a work by an unknown writer
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: An unknown author picking up a military honour and more.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British award for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', and and so on is its plain English equivalent.

clue.text: Pretty average results for gambler?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, what an ordinary gambler does, as in '..., lose some'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty average' reads together as 'fairly mediocre', but 'Pretty' is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means attractive in an appealing, innocent way, and the gambler's saying 'you win some, you lose some' gives the second sense.

clue.text: Turn towards the left, crossing river

indicators.note: the direction crosses over the river, holding it within

parts.note: on a map, west lies to the left

explanation.surface: Turning left while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: On a conventional map, west is to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to twist or wrench something forcefully, a kind of turning motion.

clue.text: Board requiring assent from two EU representatives?

parts.note: oui is yes, assent, in French
ja is yes in German; with the French word that makes assent from two EU nations

explanation.surface: An EU board that needs a yes vote from two member states.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the board really comes from French oui and German ja.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in séances to spell out supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Vessel patrolling right round European city

indicators.note: the vessel goes around the letter for right, enclosing it

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A naval vessel patrolling around a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, also called Oporto, is Portugal's second city, on the Douro.

clue.text: In the end, I'm all tired out running on this?

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of all tired are rearranged
the end of the word is its last letter

parts.note: only its final letter is used
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym-goer, exhausted after running on a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired out' reads as one phrase; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a gym machine with a moving belt, on which people run or walk.

clue.text: New grad's told to embrace also being a model of excellence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the word for also
new means made anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A new graduate is told to adopt being a model of excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New grad' suggests a fresh graduate; 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold standard is the benchmark of quality against which others are judged, named after the monetary system.
